To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
supercharged proteins enter cells through multiple endocytic routes and that their intracellular fate is related to the efficiency of macromolecular delivery.

1) the level of cellular delivery of supercharged proteins (SCP) correlates with net positive charge, 2) SCPs enter mammalian cells through multiple pathways and 3) intracellular trafficking of SCPs correlates with cellular uptake potency.
the cellular uptake mechanisms and intracellular trafficking of supercharged macromolecules is altered in a way that correlates with their delivery efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel protein-based drug and gene delivery systems.
the development of supercharged proteins as a new class of protein therapeutics.
the cellular uptake of macromolecules and their intracellular trafficking.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SCPs are a new class of protein transduction domains (PTDs) that can deliver functional macramolecules into the cytosol of mammalian cells.
the uptake mechanism of SC proteins is not only endocytosis but also macropinocytic uptake.
the uptake of supercharged proteins into mammalian cells is dependent upon the net positive charge and the structure of the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
supercharged proteins (SCP) can deliver functional molecules into the cytoplams of mammalian cells.
the cellular uptake mechanisms and endosome trafficking of SCPs can be altered by the charge and the structure of SCPs.
the cellular delivery potency of supercharged proteins is determined by their net charge and their capacity to perturb endosomal trafficking.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the intracellular delivery of macromolecules by supercharged proteins (SCP) is determined by a combination of factors including the net charge and structural features of SCP and the endosomal trafficking pathways that they engage.
supercharged GFP (SCGFP) variants enter mammalian cells through clathrin-mediated endocytosis as well as macropinocytic pathways.
supercharged GFP (SCGFP) variants can deliver functional macronolecules into the cytoplam of mammalian cells.
